verbalization: Euphoscopin C is implicated in the biological activity of Pteridine reductase 1, which is a key enzyme in the metabolism of certain complex organic compounds. This relationship is further supported by the fact that Pteridine reductase 1 acts as a target for multiple structurally distinct compounds, including (1R,6R,13R)-13-hydroxy-16,17-dimethoxy-6-prop-1-en-2-yl-2,7-dioxapentacyclo[11.8.0.03,11.04,8.014,19]henicosa-3(11),4(8),9,14,16,18-hexaen-12-one and (6S)-16-hydroxy-6-(2-hydroxypropan-2-yl)-7,11,19-trioxapentacyclo[10.8.0.02,10.04,8.013,18]icosa-1(12),2(10),3,8,13(18),14,16-heptaen-20-one. These compounds are all members of the Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3, suggesting a potential mechanism of action where Euphoscopin C may influence the activity of these transporters through the regulation of their target enzymes. The evidence suggests a possible pathway where Euphoscopin C modulates the activity of Pteridine reductase 1, which in turn affects the transport of anionic compounds across cellular membranes, potentially through interactions with Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B3.
